name: gaunt-sloth-workspace
author: Andrew Kondratev

scripts.build: pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/core run build && pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/agent run build && pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/review run build && pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/batch run build && pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/eval-reporter-junit run build && pnpm --filter @gaunt-sloth/eval-reporter-teamcity run build && pnpm --filter gaunt-sloth run build
scripts.test:embed: pnpm run build && vitest run --config vitest-embed.config.ts
scripts.it-verbose: pnpm run build && GSLOTH_IT_VERBOSE=1 node it.js
scripts.//3: OPS-39: --max-warnings 0 is what makes a warn-severity rule mean anything. Without it eslint exits 0 with warnings reported, so every such rule is decorative — which nearly demoted react-hooks/exhaustive-deps to a no-op when the recommended set (which ships it as a warning) was adopted. Keep the flag on both scripts; packages/core/spec/lintGateFailsOnWarnings.spec.ts fails if it is dropped.
scripts.//4: OPS-67: `typedoc` exits 0 with hundreds of warnings, so rendering the site in CI proves nothing on its own. `docs:check` renders it and fails on the render's own errors, on an `anchor does not exist` warning, and on DOC-STYLE rule 8's same-page anchor sweep — the ones TypeDoc reports no warning for at all. It is a step of the `test-and-lint` job in unit-tests.yml.
